incoming.name: Roald Amundsen
incoming.excerpt: In 2003 it was suggested that the plane went down northwest of Bjørnøya (Bear Island).

incoming.name: Willem Barents
incoming.excerpt: On the outward journey they sighted Bear Island and Svalbard (also known as Spitsbergen), where the ships were separated.

outgoing.name: Coal
outgoing.excerpt: Despite its remote location and barren nature, the island has seen some commercial activities in past centuries, such as coal mining, fishing and whaling.

outgoing.name: Fishing
outgoing.excerpt: Despite its remote location and barren nature, the island has seen some commercial activities in past centuries, such as coal mining, fishing and whaling.

outgoing.name: Mammal
outgoing.excerpt: There are also a few arctic foxes but no other indigenous land mammals.

outgoing.name: Moss
outgoing.excerpt: There is little plant growth, consisting mostly of moss and some scurvy grass, but no trees.

outgoing.name: Norway
outgoing.excerpt: Bjørnøya ( IPA: [ˈbjøːɳøja]), meaning "Bear Island" in Norwegian, is an arctic island of Norway that forms the southernmost part of Svalbard.

outgoing.name: Tourism
outgoing.excerpt: A small number of cruising ships have visited the island, but tourism is otherwise almost nonexistent.

outgoing.name: Walrus
outgoing.excerpt: Ringed Seal and Bearded Seal live in the waters near Bjørnøya, but the formerly common walrus has nowadays become a rare guest.

outgoing.name: Cold War
outgoing.excerpt: …in the Second World War as well as the Cold War.
